lines.text: Filigree's name means thread and grain.
lines.say: FIL-ih-gree's name means thread and grain.

lines.text: It comes from Latin filum for thread and granum for grain.
lines.say: It comes from Latin FEE-lum for thread and GRAH-num for grain.

lines.text: Filigree is fine gold or silver wire twisted and curled into lace.
The threads are soldered where they touch.
The wire can be a fraction of a millimeter thick.
Granulation adds tiny balls of gold soldered to the surface.
Mesopotamian goldsmiths made similar wire and bead work over 4,000 years ago.
lines.say: Mesopotamian goldsmiths made similar wire and bead work over four thousand years ago.

lines.text: Etruscan goldsmiths in Italy used it by the 5th century BCE.
lines.say: Etruscan goldsmiths in Italy used it by the fifth century B-C-E.

lines.text: Viking goldsmiths used it on brooches and pendants.
Malta still makes filigree, mostly in silver.
Maltese filigree often forms crosses and hearts.

post.caption: Filigree's name means thread and grain. It comes from Latin filum for thread and granum for grain. Filigree is fine gold or silver wire twisted and curled into lace. The threads are soldered where they touch. The wire can be a fraction of a millimeter thick. Granulation adds tiny balls of gold soldered to the surface. Mesopotamian goldsmiths made similar wire and bead work over 4,000 years ago. Etruscan goldsmiths in Italy used it by the 5th century BCE. Viking goldsmiths used it on brooches and pendants. Malta still makes filigree, mostly in silver. Maltese filigree often forms crosses and hearts.
